findings.title: Public findMany method removed; callers must adopt getBaseConditions + $queryRaw
findings.body: The diff replaces the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method with `getBaseConditions(): Promise<Prisma.Sql>`. The new method only returns a WHERE-clause SQL fragment; callers must now embed it in their own `prisma.$queryRaw` template and write the SELECT themselves. Any existing consumer of the service (e.g. insights API endpoints or other internal callers that previously did `service.findMany({ select: { ... } })`) will break: the method is gone, so those calls become a runtime TypeError, not just a behavior change. The PR description frames this as a test-only update and never mentions the contract change, nor does it list which callers were migrated, so it is unclear whether every callsite has been updated in lockstep.

findings.title: Caching behavior of getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions is no longer tested
findings.body: The diff deletes the entire `describe("Caching", ...)` block, which previously contained `should cache authorization conditions` and `should cache filter conditions`. The service still implements caching in `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions` (`if (this.cachedAuthConditions === undefined) { this.cachedAuthConditions = await this.buildAuthorizationConditions(); }`), but no test now exercises that branch. A future regression that accidentally rebuilds the conditions on every call would re-run the membership/team queries on every request and degrade performance without any test catching it. The caching tests should be re-added in the new `Prisma.sql` comparison style rather than dropped entirely.
